title: Serve Ops Rituals — weekly prep (scratch)
content:
Purpose: quick, practice-oriented weekly for Serve/Runtime/Infra/Console owners. Keep to 45 min. This is my scratchpad — will trim for calendar invite and add pre-reads.

Meeting length: 45 minutes (goal: surface regressions, unblock rollouts, confirm short action items)
Attendees: runtime leads, infra oncall, console PM/engineer, SRE rep (optional)
Timebox plan:
 - 0-5m: quick state + one-line wins (round robin)
 - 5-20m: top-2 operational incidents / regressions (deep dive as needed)
 - 20-35m: rollout & capacity decisions (can we push canary, burst config?)
 - 35-40m: Console UX / telemetry ask (quick prioritization)
 - 40-45m: Action items + owners + blockers

Pre-reads (attach links in invite):
 - short perf dashboard snapshot (last 24h median latency + p99)
 - KV cache eviction log sampler (last 48h)
 - Canary rollout status for model v1.2.3 (feature flag / metrics)

Agenda items (rough order):
 1) Quick wins & flags (everyone) — 2 bullets max each
    - Diego: reduced batch tail latency in test env after kernel tweak
    - Rhea: noticed a spike in console error rate when joining trace links

 2) KV cache eviction behavior (15m deep-dive)
    - Symptom: bursty eviction cycles at ~peak-traffic windows -> transient spikes in token latency
    - Hypothesis: eviction TTL + compaction runs align with the autoscaler scale-up window; compaction pauses cache retention heuristics
    - Data to surface: eviction timestamps, keys-per-eviction, concurrent requests during eviction
    - Quick asks: should we change eviction jitter to uniform(0, 30s) for a short A/B? (fast experiment)
    - Notes: risk = slightly higher memory via delayed eviction; benefit = smoother p99.

 3) Canary rollout decision for model v1.2.3 (10m)
    - Current canary at 10% traffic; p99 + error-rate looks ok but CPU tails in one AZ are concerning
    - Options: pause & investigate az-specific kernel selection vs continue and add fallback to smaller batch size
    - Quick metric to gate on: sustained p99 > 1.5x baseline for 5 minutes -> auto-rollback

 4) Console telemetry & UX (5m)
    - Rhea: customers complaining traces open to blank screen when there's >20k tokens; likely overflow in trace render pipeline
    - Quick engineering ask: add token-count guard and fallback viewer; add a flag to hide heavy traces by default in the next release

Open questions / things to chase pre-meeting:
 - Who owns the compaction jitter config? (prob infra but not 100%)
 - Is there a running experiment changing batch size heuristics in Dedicated that could be noisy?
 - Confirm if the canary is routed by region or by customer tier — matters for rolling decisions

Action items (tracked in meeting; mark owner + due date + status):
 - Aaliyah: pull eviction log samples and annotate with concurrent QPS + AZ tags; due 2026-03-14; status: open
 - Diego: run a short A/B in test env with eviction jitter uniform(0,30s) and report latency curves; due 2026-03-16; status: open
 - Rhea: implement simple token-count guard in console trace renderer (fallback to text-only view); due 2026-03-19; status: in_progress
 - Noah: validate canary routing rules and confirm whether canary is by region or by customer tier; due 2026-03-13; status: open
 - SRE oncall (TBD): add an alert that fires if p99 > 1.5x baseline for 5m during a rollout window; due 2026-03-15; status: open

Follow-up notes for myself (Aaliyah):
 - Trim this doc to 1 page, add TL;DR of key gating metrics, attach to invite.
 - Ping infra slack (#infra-ops) for compaction owner before meeting.
 - If Diego's A/B shows improvement, propose a short canary rollback protection with staggered compaction offsets.

Loose brainstorm (not for agenda unless time):
 - Consider a rolling, per-host compaction offset seed derived from host-id to avoid alignment without adding global cron randomness.
 - Explore lightweight in-memory bloom filters for cold-kv hits to avoid blind cache misses during eviction storms.

Notes-to-self: keep the meeting fast; force decisions where possible and move deep investigations to async follow-ups.
notes_summary: Scratchpad agenda for a 45m Serve Ops weekly; main focus: KV cache eviction deep-dive, canary decision for model v1.2.3, console telemetry fix. Action items listed with owners and due dates. Pre-reads: perf dashboard, eviction logs, canary status.
private_reminder: Send invite with attachments + add short TL;DR lines to calendar note. Check on compaction owner in infra slack.
